STMT-C1007C68 (customer Z45755001) uses '65 35' where every other Fred Beans statement seen uses '60 35'; '66 35' also appears elsewhere. All three are functionally identical 'original posting' rows -- the single hardcoded '60 35' silently dropped the whole original charge on any statement using a different code, falling through to the fallback-only ('99 57' reprint) row instead: invoice 9435152 on STMT-C1007C68 got checked with only the reprint's $414.62 against NetSuite's real bill total of $489.62, a false 'Amount Mismatch'. UPDATED 2026-09-18: charge/credit classification must use the CM- prefix on invoice_number, NOT which of raw_charges/raw_credits the value landed in -- confirmed live as a known extraction bug (the same invoice+amount can land in raw_charges on one row and raw_credits on another, e.g. 91488007X1's $15.34 appeared in Credits on one date and Charges on two others -- one real transaction, not three). If an invoice has a primary-code (original posting) row among its non-CM lines, use that row's amount/date and ignore every '99 57' (reprint) row for that invoice entirely. Otherwise, take the earliest date on which '99 57' rows appear and SUM(DISTINCT amount) within that single date only (confirmed live: collapses an exact pdfplumber re-extraction duplicate on 9412290X1 without merging genuinely separate aging dates on 91488007X1).

Confirmed live 2026-09-22 against STMT-D388D75F: every JR=50 row is one of two shapes, both sign-classified PAYMENT identically by statement_line.sql and indistinguishable without cross-referencing po_number against this same statement's other invoice numbers. (1) Payment-batch application: po_number matches another line's own invoice number (e.g. document 220663 recurs 53 times on this one statement, each with a different po_number pointing back to the real charge it pays off -- confirmed po_number=478828 ties to a real CHARGE line, document_number 478828, same $27.76) -- not a real NetSuite transaction, dropped outright. (2) Standalone credit: po_number matches nothing else on the statement (e.g. 491604, 489356) -- genuine vendor credits, but posted in NetSuite under 'CM<invoice>', not the raw REFER# (confirmed live: CM491604 -> $52.87 exact, CM489356 -> $196.52 exact, both entity 1760, same entity RH's real charges resolve under) -- reclassified CREDIT and CM-prefixed here, matching-time only; document_number stays the untouched raw value for display. Runs before the charge/credit split (applies_to='both'), since it's what DECIDES that split for these rows, not a dedup step within one side of it.
